name: Battle of Sedan (1870)
note: The accounts give directions only roughly (north-west, west, east, south-west). The places are set by judgement on that basis, and the Meuse, the wood and the hills are drawn only as markers; the accounts do not say exactly where each lay. They also name the Bavarian attacks both at Bazeilles and as coming from the south-west, which cannot be shown together.

terrain.name: Meuse
terrain.quote: Bavarian engineers deployed two pontoon bridges across the Meuse to secure their way across

terrain.name: Calvaire d'Illy
terrain.quote: offered a defensive position at the Calvaire d'Illy, which had both hills and woods to provide cover

terrain.name: Bois de la Garenne
terrain.quote: drove the Army of Châlons north into the Bois de la Garenne, where it was surrounded

terrain.name: Floing
terrain.quote: launching three attacks on the nearby village of Floing where the Prussian XI Corps was concentrated

terrain.name: La Moncelle
terrain.quote: the only point where that seemed possible was La Moncelle, whose flank was protected by a fortified town

sides.name: Prussian and allied Third and Fourth Armies

units.name: French 7th Corps
units.quote: MacMahon deployed Douay's 7th Corps to the north-west on the crest between the Calvaire and Floing

units.name: French 5th Corps (reserve)
units.quote: 5th Corps was placed in reserve in the centre

units.name: Margueritte's cavalry
units.quote: Ducrot directed General Jean Auguste Margueritte's cavalry squadrons to open an escape route

units.name: I Royal Bavarian Corps
units.quote: The I Royal Bavarian Corps under General Baron von der Tann moved to Bazeilles

units.name: Saxon XII Corps
units.quote: The Saxon XII Corps crossed the Meuse to the Chiers, with the Prussian Guards on their right.

units.name: Prussian Guards Corps
units.quote: with the Prussian Guards on their right

units.name: Prussian V Corps
units.quote: The Prussian V and XI Corps completed the encirclement of the French army to the north-west

units.name: Prussian XI Corps
units.quote: Prince George of Saxony and the Prussian XI Corps was assigned to the task

phases.title: The French held a ring round Sedan
phases.text: MacMahon placed the 7th Corps on the north-west crest, the 1st Corps facing east and the 12th Corps in Bazeilles, with the 5th Corps in reserve in the centre. The Germans closed a ring round the north-west, west and east.
phases.quote: The Prussian V and XI Corps completed the encirclement of the French army to the north-west by 0900 on 1 September.

phases.title: The Bavarians storm Bazeilles
phases.text: A Bavarian brigade crossed the Meuse on pontoon bridges in the morning mist and rushed Bazeilles. The French fought from stone houses while Bavarian guns shelled the buildings.
phases.quote: Von der Tann sent a brigade across pontoon bridges at 04:00 in the early morning mist, the Bavarians rushing the village and capturing it through surprise.

phases.title: Wimpffen attacks the Saxons at La Moncelle
phases.text: Ducrot ordered a retreat but Wimpffen overruled him and threw his forces against the Saxons at La Moncelle. The French rallied briefly, then the counter-attack began to collapse as fresh Prussian troops arrived.
phases.quote: Wimpffen then threw his forces against the Saxons at La Moncelle.

phases.title: French cavalry charge at Floing
phases.text: Ducrot sent Margueritte's cavalry to open an escape route with three attacks on Floing, where the XI Corps stood. Margueritte was mortally wounded in the first charge and German infantry fire defeated the other two.
phases.quote: Margueritte was mortally wounded leading the very first charge, and the two additional charges were defeated by German infantry fire at 15:00

phases.title: The Germans close in and the Bois de la Garenne falls
phases.text: German infantry reached the Calvaire and attacked from all sides. The 7th Corps broke and the 1st Corps was routed by artillery. When the Guards infantry captured the Bois de la Garenne at 14:30, the French inside surrendered.
phases.quote: when the Prussian Guards infantry captured the forest at 14:30, the French troops inside it surrendered.

phases.title: A last attack after the white flag
phases.text: Napoleon III hoisted a white flag on the walls of Sedan. Wimpffen refused to surrender and launched one more attack, which the Germans defeated.
phases.quote: Wimpffen saw the white flag but refused to surrender and launched one more attack, which was defeated by the Germans.
